sub_questions: What are llm-d's components (inference scheduler / Endpoint Picker (EPP), Gateway API Inference Extension integration, proxy/gateway layer such as Envoy/kgateway/Istio/agentgateway, KV-cache manager/indexer, prefix-cache and load-aware scorers, P/D disaggregation routing sidecar, model-service Helm charts, vLLM integration), and which of them are coupled to Kubernetes pods vs. reusable independently?

How does the llm-d router discover, represent, and track backends today (InferencePool selector over pod labels, EPP datastore/pod reconciler, metrics scraping, endpoint identity, ext-proc protocol with the proxy, destination-endpoint header), and where exactly is the Kubernetes-pod assumption baked in?

What extension seams exist in the router for customization (scheduling framework plugins: filters, scorers, pickers, profile handlers, pre-request/post-response hooks; pluggable data layer / data sources / endpoint discovery; configuration via EndpointPickerConfig), and do any of them already allow non-pod endpoints?

What upstream work, proposals, issues, or releases in llm-d and the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension address non-pod or external backends (standalone EPP mode, static/file endpoint lists, endpoint discovery abstraction, multi-cluster InferencePool, non-k8s deployments)?

What kinds of 'backends other than k8s pods' are realistic targets (VMs and bare-metal vLLM/SGLang hosts, containers under Docker/Podman/Nomad, Slurm/HPC jobs, remote clusters, external or managed OpenAI-compatible endpoints, serverless GPU providers) and what does each require from the router (metrics endpoint, KV-cache events, health, auth, network reachability)?

What candidate strategies exist for supporting non-pod backends while maximizing llm-d reuse — e.g. (a) model non-pod backends as Kubernetes objects (selectorless Service + manual EndpointSlice, virtual-kubelet/virtual pods, placeholder pods), (b) implement a custom endpoint-discovery/datastore source inside EPP via plugin or thin fork, (c) run EPP in standalone mode with its own endpoint source, (d) use an Envoy ext-proc + ORIGINAL_DST setup directly with EPP, (e) build a custom router that imports llm-d libraries (scheduling framework, kv-cache indexer) as Go modules, (f) contribute a discovery abstraction upstream?

How do these strategies compare on reuse of llm-d components, fork/maintenance burden and upstream divergence, feature parity (prefix-aware routing, KV-cache-aware routing, load-aware scoring, P/D disaggregation, flow control/fairness), operational complexity, latency, and failure handling?
Which strategy should be recommended, with what implementation roadmap, and what risks and open questions remain given llm-d's and GIE's upstream trajectory?

levers.domain_notes: Sourcing: primary sources are the GitHub repos and docs of llm-d (llm-d/llm-d, llm-d-inference-scheduler, llm-d-kv-cache-manager, routing sidecar) and kubernetes-sigs/gateway-api-inference-extension — source code, design proposals under docs/proposals, issues, merged PRs, and release notes; academic literature is thin and secondary. Evidence norms: code at HEAD and merged PRs outrank design docs, which outrank vendor blogs and conference talks; flag any claim that depends on an unmerged proposal. Recency window: last 12-18 months — llm-d and GIE APIs changed quickly (InferencePool v1 GA, EPP plugin/data-layer refactors), so prefer the newest release and date every API-shape claim.
